statement: Carry-free reduction and tail theorem: for every prime p, p does not divide binomial(2n,n) exactly when every base-p digit of n is at most (p-1)/2, equivalently n mod p^j<p^j/2 for all j. The total reciprocal mass of all such primes p>sqrt(2n) is bounded by an absolute constant. The remaining p<=sqrt(2n) problem cannot be reduced to a single prime-power test, a summable exponent annulus, pairwise incompatibility, full-period CRT independence, a common smaller integer, or a local nonnegative Legendre-jump certificate. Any closing lemma must instead be a cutoff-aware quantitative rigidity theorem for a growing weighted family of prime bases, consistent with the EGRS infinite two-base construction.
